questions.question: Which three modular decomposition styles are mentioned as ways to structure system specifications?
questions.explanation:
The context states that a specification may be structured around the objects manipulated by the system, the functions performed by the system, or the events processed by the system [Page 23].

---

questions.question: Why does making document sections modular improve changeability, according to the text?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any external references.
options.B: It allows individual sections to be changed or replaced without affecting other parts.
options.C: It guarantees that all sections use the same font and shading.
options.D: It forces all requirements to be written in natural language.

questions.explanation:
The passage explains that changeability is achieved by minimizing external references and making document sections as modular as possible, so individual sections can be changed without impacting others [Page 34].

---

questions.question: In a structured approach to specifying requirements, what is the primary role of standard templates?

options.A: To enforce uniformity across the specification.
options.C: To define the programming language syntax used.

questions.explanation:
The text notes that defining standard templates for requirements imposes some uniformity on the specification [Page 23].

questions.question: Which modular decomposition style focuses on “what the system does”?
questions.explanation:
The context lists “functions performed by the system” as one of the ways a specification can be structured, indicating a focus on the system’s actions [Page 23].

---

questions.question: Which modular decomposition style groups requirements based on the entities the system manipulates?
questions.explanation:
The passage mentions structuring the specification around “the objects manipulated by the system,” which groups requirements by entities [Page 23].

---

questions.question: Which modular decomposition style is concerned with “the occurrences the system responds to”?
questions.explanation:
The text includes “events processed by the system” as a possible structuring focus, indicating a style based on occurrences [Page 23].

questions.question: How does structuring a specification around objects affect its organization?

options.A: It groups requirements by the functions they perform.
options.B: It groups requirements by the events they trigger.
options.C: It groups requirements by the objects they involve.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any templates.

questions.explanation:
By structuring around objects, the specification organizes requirements according to the objects they involve, as described in the passage [Page 23].

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct benefit of using modular document sections, as described in the context?

options.A: Reducing the total number of pages in the document.
options.B: Allowing sections to be edited independently without side effects on other sections.
options.C: Ensuring all sections use identical wording.
options.D: Making the document readable only by experts.

questions.explanation:
The passage states that modular sections enable individual sections to be changed and replaced without affecting other parts [Page 34].

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the relationship between modular decomposition and changeability?

options.A: More modular decomposition always increases the number of external references.
options.B: Modular decomposition reduces changeability because sections become interdependent.
options.C: Modular decomposition enhances changeability by minimizing external references and isolating sections.
options.D: Changeability is unrelated to how a specification is modularized.

questions.explanation:
The text links modular decomposition with changeability, noting that minimizing external references and modular sections improve the ability to change parts independently [Page 34].

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a modular decomposition style in the provided context?
questions.explanation: The context only mentions objects, functions, and events as decomposition styles; “layers” are not cited [Page 23].
